# Geometric audit of the symmetric triangle-chain sector reduction

I checked the complete arguments in
candidate 58714b1fac606069 and
candidate 9c420d2e51075e2c against the
actual finite-fiber measure. The geometric and analytic reductions PASS.
This audit does not certify the separately stated rational inequality(S).

## Original normals and actual center

The selected point is the original peak fiber's own centroid
(0,R/3,R/3), a deterministic actual source point. The touching radius
majorant is r_j<=R, with zero slope. In the archived barycentric swap,
u_i<0 gives u_i(r_j-R)>=0; dropping that term produces one genuine
positive-normal ambient cap of no larger mass on every original fiber.
Thus mixed-sign and all-negative normals are covered. Whole boundary
fibers of vertical caps are retained in the finite-tilt domination;
they are not declared null. Nonvertical cut boundaries have zero planar
area. Positive coordinate permutation is an actual common ambient
symmetry. The subsequent normal form( a,1-a),a>=1/2 loses no original
cap relevant to the lower bound.

## Exact one-direction pair calculation

The piecewise triangular tail has matching values and first derivatives.
In normalized height coordinates(0,c,1), proper straddling minimizers
have c>1/2,1/2<=q<=c, shift(c-q)/(2c-1), and cost
1-(2q-1)^2/(2c-1). The support and straddling conditions follow directly
from those inequalities. Every other regime yields a concave quadratic,
a zero-shift convex quadratic, a monotone full/empty transition, or the
full/empty plateau. Thus there are no omitted boundary minima.

For a>=2/3, c<=1/2, and F_{a,r}(R/3)/r^2<=1/2 for every r<=R:
at r=R the latter is equivalent to a>=2/3, and decreasing r only raises
the normalized threshold. Consequently every pair is minimized at shift
zero, and beta=0 realizes all minima simultaneously. The exact sector
formula follows. For the low sector, half of the pair floor is exactly
A(r-c_a)_+^2-L(r-rho_a)_+^2. The own surplus is precisely
(2-3a)R^2/[9(1-a)]. The equal-normal endpoint formula is the direct
one-piece projection calculation, including r=2R/3.

## Corrected hinge and inverse-radius comparison

The primitive of6(r-2/3)_+-r^2 is nonpositive and ends at zero.
A concave nonincreasing polygonal radius leg has nondecreasing outward
drops. On each nonconstant segment its inverse-radius density is the
reciprocal drop, hence nondecreasing as a function of radius. Its extension
by zero below the endpoint is a nonnegative nondecreasing finite step
function. Initial zero slopes occur only at radiusR and contribute a
nonnegative plateau term. This justifies the upper-interval indicator
decomposition without differentiating a possibly noninvertible function.

The square's unit-cell trapezoid error is delta^2/6, and the positive
hinge's is nonnegative. The exact symmetric endpoint correction is
sum_all f=2T_f+f(b), not2T_f-f(b). The lower bound
f(b)-(1-b)^2/3>=-13/27 is correct on both scalar intervals, with minimum
at b=2/3. The cap bonus1/9 leaves the claimed1/243 positive term.

For the intermediate kernel, k(r)/r^2 is increasing on every piece and
continuous at both joins. Its r^2-weighted average on[0,1] is
lambda=3integral k. Hence k-lambda r^2 changes sign only from negative
to positive and has zero integral, so every upper-interval integral is
nonnegative. The same step-density representation proves the polygonal
comparison exactly, including plateaus and truncation at a positive
endpoint. The strict inequality lambda>2/9 follows from the factored
rational expression on the stated a interval.

## Trapezoid comparison of the remaining negative curvature

The identity L-A=B makes
k+B(r-rho)_+^2=A[(r-c)_+^2-(r-rho)_+^2] convex. Its derivative is
continuous; its second derivative is2A between c and rho and zero
elsewhere. Thus its trapezoid error is nonnegative on every cell.

For convex C1 H, the error on endpoints u>w is
[2(u-w)]^{-1} integral_w^u(s-w)(u-s)H''(s) ds. Applied to squared
positive parts, H'' is the ordinary bounded piecewise function2*1_{s>rho};
there is no missing derivative-jump atom. Each local bridge kernel is
at most the kernel on the full endpoint interval[b,1], because the
kernel increases when either interval endpoint is moved outward.
Integration over the disjoint radius intervals therefore proves
sum cell_errors(H)<=error(H;1,b). Zero drops contribute zero and may
be omitted. This establishes the coarse-interval error bound for any
number of cells and every concave polygonal leg.

The resulting endpoint error E(b) has exactly the two formulas stated
in the source, with agreement at b=rho and value zero at b=1.
The exact square mass identity then gives the unconditional bound(13).
No integral is substituted for mixed mass without its finite error.

## Conditional scalar bounds and small supports

The own cap yields M>M0 under a strict failure. The pointwise comparison
(r-rho)_+ <=[(1-rho)/(1-c)](r-c)_+ has the correct direction and is
equivalent to r<=1 above rho. The simplified positive coefficient
K=a(6a-1)/(3a-1)^2 is correct. Using the independently proved quadratic
truncation theorem yields cap/V>=vM+g, and therefore M>M1 when a<alpha.
For a>=alpha, this already reaches2M/9.

When there are at least two reflected pairs, concavity indeed implies
r1>=(1+b)/2 and r2>=b, so M>=3/2+b+(5/2)b^2. No such bound is used
for one pair. That case is covered at this same middle centroid by the
archived three-homothetic-fiber theorem: a heavy middle uses its own
centroid, and otherwise the theorem selects that centroid; neither
symmetric endpoint can be a half-mass heavy fiber. A single fiber is
immediate from ordinary triangle Grünbaum.

The exact sector verifier passed9149 rational pair, chamber, sequence,
and shared-tilt checks. These are supplementary algebra checks; the
arguments above justify the entire continuous parameter ranges.
